engine.verdict:
The money parts of PR #52 hold up. I found no blocker and no major issue. The mutation result is still missing: I had to report before the packets-explain shard finished, so it needs a re-run or a read of the report before merge.

**No arithmetic in the renderer.**
- The renderer is packages/packets/src/explain plus explainPacket. `formatFigure` only formats text: `formatUsd(parseCents)`, `formatUnroundedUsd`, appending `%` or ` per RVU`, verbatim, and an array's length.
- Its choices between wordings use string equality only.
- `purity.test.ts` reads the code's syntax tree and fails on any arithmetic operator, size comparison, negation, `decimal(`, `BigInt`, `Number(` or `Date`.
- Every figure is read through the fixed `SLOTS` table of trace and citation paths. I checked the paths by hand; each points to the right stored value.

**Flags and Medicare rules (orchestrator line 2).**
- A flag that is off reads only "Not applied (flag off)".
- The payer copy prints no flag at all. Adjustment steps whose flag is off are left out.
- An omitted timed-units rule defaults to UNKNOWN, so "the contract follows Medicare's pooled rule" appears only when a specialist entered it.
- On a Medicare Advantage non-contracted line the words say "Medicare's reductions … under 42 CFR 422.214" and use Medicare's own timed-units text. The contract adjustment is null there and rounding never comes from a rate record. One unreachable table entry still says "the rate record's rule" (nit below).

**The year (line 3).** The year is worded from `steps.fee_schedule.lookup`. `checkYearBasis` refuses a trace whose lookup, year basis and label disagree.

**The worksheet (line 4).** It prints RVUs, GPCIs, the conversion factor, the percentage and the per-unit parts at the percentage, all from `unit_cents` in the trace. It prints no product of an RVU and its GPCI, no total RVU and no amount at 100%. The golden test computes those values independently and asserts none of them is printed.

**SHA-256 check before printing.** explainPacket hashes each stored trace with the same `traceSha256` the content uses before it parses or words anything. It refuses a missing trace, a different trace, an unpriced trace, a different rate record and a regulation citation on a line that is not Medicare Advantage. The export job does this before anything is decrypted. `approveOnce` refuses a version the renderer cannot word.

**WORDS_VERSION guards.**
- They are present at approve and at the export request (`requireWordsVersion`) and in the export job (`payload.words_version`).
- The residual gap the design names is real: approved under renderer A, a deploy, then exported under B passes. Attest has no guard.
- The guards can wrongly refuse after a deploy and can be silently bypassed by a sentence edit (two minor findings below).

**The four surfaces.** The line page, builder, review and PDF all call the same renderer. The review and the PDF both use the payer audience. The PDF matches its words to rows by index.

**Golden claims.**
- I checked by hand: G01 (21.12 per unit, 31.448 after the multiple procedure payment reduction, 30.75656 after sequestration, rounded to 30.76; worksheet parts 6.20, 13.49, 1.43), G02 (23.232, 27.038 and 29.70 at 110%), G07 (77% assistant reduction to 16.2624), G124 (lesser of) and G141 (per visit).
- All match their traces and the fixtures/golden worksheets.
- Test runs:
  - The explain tests (10 files, 466 tests) pass.
  - The golden project tests (319, including G01 and G02 against their worksheets and the trace pins) pass.

**Payer copy and viewer.**
- The payer copy's scan for internal terms and code shapes runs on the payer words and worksheets in both the golden and the property tests. A grep of every payer pin finds no "rate record", "engine", "release" or "flag".
- The viewer gets words built on the server: no trace, no recorded steps, no date (`dated()` guards every date path).
- The unpriced reasons' meaning and remedy are tested word for word against docs/product/unpriced-reasons.md, and remedies.ts now derives from that one table.

**Test strength.** A renderer that printed a recomputed amount different from the stored one would fail three ways: the by-source check re-reads the path and formats it with an independent formatter, the token check finds a number in no trace leaf, and the golden pins move. A recomputation that happens to equal the stored value is not detectable by output, but the syntax-tree purity test blocks it.

**Mutation shard (incomplete).** The packets-explain shard instrumented 1,970 mutants in 9 files, and its initial run passed (417 tests). I was told to report before it finished, so I have no score and no survivor list. The output will land in /home/user/figures-in-words/reports/mutation/packets-explain/ and the log is /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-PhysicalTherapy/cd4c3776-ffb4-50ed-99cf-e6bf837d5699/scratchpad/fiw-review/stryker-packets-explain.log.

**Coverage.** New behaviour has golden pins (more than 100 claims), a property test (100 generated claims across every method, flag combination and audience) and fixtures CAS-30 to CAS-34.

Progress notes are in /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-PhysicalTherapy/cd4c3776-ffb4-50ed-99cf-e6bf837d5699/scratchpad/fiw-review/progress/payment-engine.md.

findings.title: Export job refuses a stale words version as 'The PDF could not be printed.', retries it twice, and blocks a fresh request in the meantime
findings.evidence: apps/worker/src/packets/export.ts:302 throws PacketExportRenderError, which exportFailureCode maps to 'render_failed'. apps/web/src/lib/packets/export-attempts.ts:63 shows 'The PDF could not be printed.'. apps/worker/src/jobs/registry.ts:113 sets retryLimit 2, so a mismatch that can never succeed is retried. registry.test.ts:81 asserts the singleton key ignores words_version, so a request after the deploy is treated as already queued while the old job retries. The remedy the design states ('request the export again') is never shown.
findings.fix: Give the mismatch its own failure code, e.g. 'words_changed' with the text 'The calculation's wording changed since the export was requested. Request it again.'. Fail it without retry (record it as a refusal, or throw pg-boss's non-retry error) so the singleton is released at once.

findings.title: WORDS_VERSION moves on a sentence change only if RENDERER_REVISION is bumped by hand, so the three guards can be silently bypassed
findings.evidence: packages/packets/src/words-version.ts hashes only WORD_TABLES, SLOTS and RENDERER_REVISION. Any text literal in explain/line.ts or explain/worksheet.ts (e.g. 'Each later unit loses …') can change without moving WORDS_VERSION. version.test.ts checks tables and slots only. Commit f1dcd8ea did bump it by hand, but nothing enforces the bump.
findings.fix: In version.test.ts, pin the SHA-256 of the source text of explain/{line,worksheet,figures}.ts next to RENDERER_REVISION (a test-only constant), so any edit to those files fails until both are rewritten. Alternatively, fold a hash of the golden pins into the check.

findings.title: Medicare Advantage rounding table words a rule as 'the rate record’s rule'
findings.evidence: packages/packets/src/explain/words.ts, MEDICARE_ROUNDING_ORIGIN_TEXT.rate_record = 'the rate record’s rule'. The entry is unreachable today because MA_NONCONTRACTED_TERMS.rounding is null (packages/contracts/src/terms.ts:358-363, engine.ts:900), but it contradicts the rule that Medicare's rules on such a line are never a rate record's.
findings.fix: Have roundingStep throw ExplainShapeError when words.medicare is true and origin is 'rate_record', and remove that entry from the Medicare table.

findings.title: Payer copy prints Medicare reductions on a commercial line without saying the contract adopts them
findings.evidence: line.ts termsStep returns only the method sentence for the payer. In the G07 payer pin, the payer reads 'Modifier CQ …: Medicare’s assistant percentage is 77% of the amount.' with no statement that the contract incorporates the assistant reduction. The internal words do say 'Applied, as the rate record’s flags are on'.
findings.fix: For the payer, add one sentence when a flag is on, worded as the contract: 'The contract applies Medicare’s assistant reduction.' Still print nothing for flags that are off.

findings.title: Doc comment says exact_dollars keeps every fraction digit, but trailing zeros are dropped
findings.evidence: packages/packets/src/explain/figures.ts header ('every fraction digit kept'). formatUnroundedUsd (packages/money/src/cents.ts:86) strips trailing zeros of the fraction. The value is unchanged.
findings.fix: Reword the comment to say trailing zeros of the fraction of a cent are dropped.

ux.verdict:
Request changes. One blocker, then a few should-fix items; the change itself is a big improvement. The line trace page no longer shows raw JSON, bare method codes or cents. Viewers now get the calculation in words, and no date appears inside the trace. The packet builder, the packet review and the payer's PDF print the same payer words, checked row by row on p.packet.default.1280, p.packet-review.default.1280 and screens-after/pdf-pages/page-3.png. Figures are in mono with tabular numerals, and money is formatted from cents. Long amounts and hashes wrap at 390 px on the packet and review pages. Dark contrast is fine (muted #A7B1C2 on #0B1626 is about 8:1). `pnpm lint:copy` passed under the lock: 503 files read, no findings. The p.case.* and p.line.empty-not-priced.* pairs differ only in IDs, timestamps and which synthetic line was chosen, so the PR does not change them, and nothing else regressed between before and after.

The blocker: at the PR head (a2eee987) the line trace page is still 509 px wide at a 390 px viewport, and the PR's own new phone-width checks fail on it in CI.

Other things to know:
- The worktree /home/user/figures-in-words has an uncommitted, unpushed edit to the line page (break-all on its IDs and hashes). It was not made by this review. It may be the fix for the blocker, but it is not on the PR.
- No tour shot shows a fee-schedule worksheet, an unpriced line's words or a words refusal, because the synthetic data has none of them. Those were checked against the code and pricing.spec only.

On the baseline review's raw findings for these screens:
- **Fixed by this PR:**
  - narrow-practice-1-06: raw JSON is now under words, in a closed disclosure inside a named, focusable scroller.
  - a11y-practice-1-16: fixed for the line page's trace blocks.
  - narrow-practice-1-05: fixed for the calculation per line, since its Trace SHA-256 table column is gone. The Versions table hashes remain, and they belong to the shared hash-component PR.
- **This PR should fix now (its own files, same kind of problem):**
  - narrow-practice-1-02: the 390 px overflow (the blocker).
  - a11y-practice-1-14: the step titles and the review's calculation need real headings; its notes said this PR should do it.
- **Not now:**
  - flows-practice-13 (links from a line to its case): navigation, not wording; it can ride with #107.
  - flows-practice-35 (an amount summary on the PDF cover): new cover content, which needs the ADR 0058 cover baseline redone; a separate PR.
  - a11y-practice-2-18 (untagged PDFs): audit #103, Lane A's PR 7.
  - a11y-practice-1-08 (the sticky header can hide focus): app-wide fix in brand.css, outside this PR's files.

findings.title: The line trace page still scrolls sideways at 390 px, and the PR's own new phone-width e2e checks fail on it
findings.evidence: Shots p.line.default.390 and p.line.viewer.390 are 509 px wide after the PR (they were before too). Tile screens-after p.line.default.390-00 shows the Rule release value '900001 (manifest 6d346c8f...cdbce45a)' running past the card. CI check-run 121404954151 'e2e (2/2)' at a2eee987 fails 2 tests at apps/web/e2e/a11y.ts:57: pricing.spec.ts:25 (the PR added atPhoneWidth on 'the line trace page, its fee schedule record open') and viewer-phi.spec.ts:70 (the PR added 'the viewer's line trace'). Both report 'no sideways scroll at 390 px' with overflowing ['span.font-mono.text-xs (right 509)'] and scrollWidth 509. Cause: apps/web/src/app/p/[practiceId]/lines/[lineId]/page.tsx (head line ~137, base :109) prints the 64-character manifest SHA-256 in a span that cannot break. An uncommitted break-all edit for these spans is sitting in the review worktree and is not on the PR.
findings.fix: Commit the fix to the PR: let every hash and ID on this page break (overflow-wrap:anywhere / break-all), or better, the shared hash component from narrow-practice-1-02. Then re-run e2e (2/2) and retake p.line.*.390. Those shots must come out 390 px wide.

'per_visit' and 'ncci_ptp' fall back to labelOf ('Per visit', 'NCCI PTP'; titleOf at view.ts:97-99) between Step 3 and Step 4. lineTraceSteps (view.ts:222-232) drops steps without words for the viewer, so p.line.viewer.1280 reads Step 3, 'NCCI PTP', Step 5. findings.title: The builder's card text and the reviewer's checklist promise a 'fee schedule worksheet' that most lines don't have

On p.packet.default.1280 and p.packet-review.default.1280 every row is a fixed schedule and no worksheet exists. The attester is asked to confirm something that is not on the page.

findings.title: The payer's words repeat figures: patient share twice per PDF row, observed allowed three times per row, and '$100.00 becomes $100.00' when rounding changed nothing
findings.evidence: screens-after/pdf-pages/page-3.png: each row has 'Patient share $14.00, reported beside the expected amount and never subtracted from it.' in the words and '$14.00, reported, never subtracted' in the Patient share column. The summary says 'observed allowed $70.00; short $30.00', and the last bullet says 'Observed allowed $70.00 ... Expected $100.00, observed allowed $70.00: short $30.00.' The same appears on the builder and review (p.packet.default.390 tiles 02-03). Each row comes to about 10 lines at 390 px.
findings.fix: In packages/packets/src/explain/line.ts, leave the patient-share sentence out of the payer audience's steps (the PDF has its own column), or drop the column. Let the variance step state only the basis ('the allowed amount the remittance states'), since the summary already gives the short. When rounded equals unrounded, write 'needed no rounding: $100.00'. Pin the change in the golden words.

findings.title: The internal and viewer words still carry bare codes
findings.evidence: p.line.default.1280 tile 01: 'Patient share $14.00 (PR 2 $14.00)' (line.ts patientShareStep, the CAS group and reason in verbatim form), 'MUE not checked (flag off).', 'NCCI edits not checked (flag off).', the step title 'NCCI PTP', and 'the payer's allowed amount (AMT B6)'. The viewer sees MUE and NCCI unexpanded too (p.line.viewer.1280 tile 00). The payer variant writes these out, so the practice's own readers get less plain words than the payer.
findings.fix: On first use, write each initialism out with the code after it: 'the medically unlikely edit (MUE)', 'National Correct Coding Initiative (NCCI) edits'. Name the CAS pair ('PR 2, the deductible, $14.00'), or point to the Adjustments table. Keep the code as a code segment after the words.

findings.title: Fourteen identical disclosure summaries with small touch targets

A screen-reader user tabbing hears 'As the engine recorded it' 14 times with no step named. The summary is about 16 px tall at 390 px (p.line.default.390-01). It is keyboard-operable (native details) and has the global :focus-visible ring (apps/web/src/app/brand.css:52).
